name: Anarsa
subtitle: ghee-fried discs of soaked ground rice and jaggery, crusted with sesame

ingredients.qty: 600 ml, for deep-frying, plus 2 tbsp for the dough

ingredients.note: only if the dough will not come together
traditional in some households in place of half the sesame

prepNotes: Soak the rice in cold water for 3 days, changing the water every morning and evening, then drain it and spread it on a cloth in the shade for 2 hours until damp-dry, not crisp.
Grind the damp rice to a fine flour and sieve it; any coarse grit will tear the discs in the oil.
Mix the dough and rest it covered for at least 24 hours, and up to 4 days. This rest is what gives anarsa its honeycomb inside, and it cannot be skipped.
Have the sesame in a wide plate and your hands greased before you shape.

steps.text: Rub the grated jaggery into the ground rice flour with your fingertips until it looks like damp sand, 5 minutes.
steps.tip: No water. The moisture in the jaggery and the damp flour is all the dough gets.

steps.text: Work in 2 tbsp ghee and the crushed cardamom and knead to a stiff dough that just holds when squeezed; add the milk a teaspoon at a time only if it crumbles.
Cover and rest the dough at room temperature for 24 hours, by which time it will have softened and smell faintly fermented.
Pinch off lime-sized balls, press each one into the plate of sesame, and flatten to a 7cm disc about 6mm thick, sesame side up.
steps.tip: Keep them thick. Thin anarsa disintegrates the moment it hits the ghee.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a kadhai to a gentle 160C. A crumb of dough should rise slowly with fine bubbles, not fizz.
steps.tip: Anarsa is fried low and slow. Hot ghee browns the jaggery before the middle cooks.

steps.text: Slide in one disc, sesame side down, and fry undisturbed for 90 seconds until it lifts and floats.
Spoon hot ghee over the top rather than turning it, and fry a further 3 to 4 minutes until deep reddish-brown and the bubbling slows.
steps.tip: Fry two at a time at most. Crowding drops the temperature and they break apart.

steps.text: Lift each anarsa out with a slotted spoon and stand it on edge against the side of a colander to drain for 5 minutes.
Cool completely before eating. They crisp as they cool and are fragile while hot.

storage: Stores 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature. Do not refrigerate; the jaggery weeps and the discs go soft.
